captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a rectangular, flat-pack box designed for laser cutting, featuring interlocking finger joints (tenons) along all edges. The front panel has a series of small, rectangular cutouts spaced evenly for rocker switches, with engraved text labels positioned below each cutout. The back panel features larger, specialized cutouts with mounting holes to accommodate electrical sockets like IEC power entries and outlets. The side, top, and bottom panels lock the box together, forming a sturdy, modular enclosure for a power strip.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric, laser-cuttable power supply box in OpenSCAD with interlocking tenon joints. The box should dynamically adjust its width based on a string of socket types (e.g., 'EOOO' for entry and outlets) and include custom switch cutouts on the front panel with corresponding engraved text labels.
captions.factory: The script defines modular components for different socket shapes (socket_euro, socket_schuko, socket_entry, socket_outlet) and a toggle switch cutout. It calculates box dimensions (w, h, d) and tenon counts based on material thickness 't' and the length of the 'sockets' string. The panels (top, bottom, front, back, side) are constructed using difference() operations between flat cubes and arrays of smaller cubes representing the interlocking finger slots, while the front panel uses a loop to subtract the switch cutouts and render text using the write() helper.
